::: {#fig-best-constant-step}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: best-constant-step-plot-r
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the error factor against the step length, from 0 to 1.
#|   A solid blue curve falls in a straight line from 1 at a step length of 0
#|   to a sharp minimum of 0.5 at a step length of 0.5,
#|   then rises in a straight line, crossing 1 at a step length of 0.667
#|   and reaching 2 at a step length of 1.
#|   A dotted horizontal line marks 1.
#|   A dashed vermilion vertical line marks 0.5.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
bcs_grid_pf <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 401)
bcs_first_pf <- abs(1 - 3 * bcs_grid_pf)
bcs_second_pf <- abs(1 - bcs_grid_pf)
bcs_rho_pf <- pmax(bcs_first_pf, bcs_second_pf)
bcs_curve_pf <- tibble::tibble(s = bcs_grid_pf, rho = bcs_rho_pf)
bcs_aes_pf <- ggplot2::aes(s, rho)
ggplot2::ggplot(bcs_curve_pf, bcs_aes_pf) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "#0072B2") +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0.5, colour = "#D55E00", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Step length", y = "Error factor")
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: best-constant-step-plot-python
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   Plot of the error factor against the step length, from 0 to 1.
#|   A solid blue curve falls in a straight line from 1 at a step length of 0
#|   to a sharp minimum of 0.5 at a step length of 0.5,
#|   then rises in a straight line, crossing 1 at a step length of 0.667
#|   and reaching 2 at a step length of 1.
#|   A dotted horizontal line marks 1.
#|   A dashed vermilion vertical line marks 0.5.
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 5
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

bcs_grid_pf = np.linspace(0, 1, 401)
bcs_rho_pf = np.maximum(np.abs(1 - 3 * bcs_grid_pf), np.abs(1 - bcs_grid_pf))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 4), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(bcs_grid_pf, bcs_rho_pf, color="#0072B2")
ax.axhline(1, color="black", linestyle=":")
ax.axvline(0.5, color="#D55E00", linestyle="--")
ax.set_xlabel("Step length")
ax.set_ylabel("Error factor")
plt.show()
```

:::

The factor $\convrate(\steplen)$ of @exm-best-constant-step against the [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $\steplen$ (solid).
The best step length (dashed) is where the curve is lowest,
and the [bound](sets.qmd#def-bound) on the [error](#def-iterate-error) shrinks only where the curve is below $1$ (dotted).

:::
